transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Kim: Hi everyone, thanks for taking the time. i'm Jordan Kim, AE at Redwood. with me is Priya Patel, our solutions engineer, and Maya from customer success. how's everyone?
[00:12] Alex Rivera: Hey Jordan, yeah thanks. Alex here, CTO at Lumen Systems. we have Sara, Tom, Priya (PM) on as well.
[00:20] Jordan Kim: Great. quick agenda: understand your use case, current stack, what success looks like, and then walk through the PLG quickstart experience — free credits, SDKs, and time-to-first-token. any additions?
[00:30] Sara Chen: that's perfect. main thing for us is evaluating hosted first; want to know how fast we can get from signup to a token and to a quick proof-of-concept. also want a sense of when we should consider Dedicated or Private.
[00:42] Priya Patel: cool — i'll also cover perf expectations, batching, caching, and how we recommend running initial benchmarks.
[00:50] Tom O'Neill: i want to confirm networking limitations: can we do VPC peering or do we need an on-prem option for certain clients?
[00:58] Jordan Kim: good, we'll go through that.
[01:05] Jordan Kim: quick background check — are you currently using any hosted LLM APIs? OpenAI, Anthropic, or self-hosted?
[01:12] Alex Rivera: We have some POCs on OpenAI for assistant features, but for productization we need more control and predictable cost. we've also experimented with a self-hosted cluster but ops cost got high.
[01:25] Sara Chen: our success criteria: sub-150ms token latency for short completions, predictable cost per 1k tokens, and SOC2-level auditability for customer data.
[01:36] Jordan Kim: great. on SOC2 and audit logs — Redwood is SOC2 compliant and provides audit logs, SSO/SAML, RBAC, and KMS integrations. for Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS/HSM.
[01:48] Sara Chen: when you say "time-to-first-token" for PLG, what's realistic?
[01:53] Priya Patel: for the typical PLG flow it's pretty fast — sign up, redeem free credits, API key in the console, run the quickstart with SDK or cURL. most teams see first token within 5-15 minutes depending on verifying billing and DNS steps. i've seen internal users do it sub-5 if they skip some steps.
[02:10] Alex Rivera: ok that's useful. what about quotas and rate limits for free credits?
[02:16] Jordan Kim: free credits default has conservative rate limits but we can temporarily lift them for an evaluation or pilot. also, quickstart templates include sample requests and batching guidance.
[02:28] Tom O'Neill: curious about when Dedicated makes sense. cost vs latency?
[02:33] Priya Patel: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput. it's ideal once you need sustained high throughput or strict latency SLOs. Hosted is great for time-to-market and early PLG usage; Dedicated is for commit-based steady usage.
[02:46] Jordan Kim: think of it as hosted for exploration and early productization; dedicated when you need throughput predictability or data isolation. Private if you have strict residency or air-gapped requirements.
[02:57] Sara Chen: can you run benchmarks on our workloads? we'd want to compare OpenAI latency/cost vs Redwood hosted using one of your open models.
[03:05] Priya Patel: yes — we normally provide a benchmark checklist and runbook. we'll ask you to provide sample prompts and a small dataset. we can run on hosted up to a point; for dedicated-level benchmarking we'll spin up a dedicated eval environment.
[03:20] Alex Rivera: any notes on model quantization? we want to reduce cost but not lose output quality.
[03:26] Priya Patel: quantization is effective for cost but results vary by model and prompt. Redwood Optimize suggests quant profiles and we can recommend 8-bit quant or int4 for some models — but we'll validate on your prompt set. sometimes you get minimal quality loss, sometimes you see regressions, so we tie that to evaluation metrics.
[03:44] Speaker 1: there's also caching, prefix caching or KV cache that can reduce token costs for repeated context.
[03:50] Sara Chen: right — that's important for our chat histories.
[03:54] Jordan Kim: quick note on networking and Private: with VPC/private deployments we support VPC peering and customer-managed networking; for fully air-gapped environments we have an on-prem package but that's a longer procurement conversation.
[04:07] Tom O'Neill: and KMS? we need to ensure keys never leave our control for certain customers.
[04:12] Priya Patel: we support integrations with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and even HSM solutions for Private. Hosted has encryption at rest but for some customers we recommend Dedicated with customer-managed KMS or Private.
[04:24] Alex Rivera: good. talk to me about logs and retention? compliance requires at least 1 year of logs for audit.
[04:30] Jordan Kim: audit logs can be retained per customer settings; we have add-on packages for long-term retention.
[04:36] Sara Chen: got it. next — how much work to get a quick POC?
[04:40] Priya Patel: usually our PLG quickstart has a sample repo and SDK snippets. with free credits you can do a POC in under a day — realistically 1-2 days to integrate from a dev perspective, and then iterative tuning.
[04:52] Alex Rivera: what's included in the free credits?
[04:55] Jordan Kim: free credits cover API usage for a fixed amount, enough to run small to medium PoCs. they also unlock the console, model catalog, and basic observability. the credits are time-limited and we can extend for pilots.
[05:08] Tom O'Neill: will the free trial let us test multi-turn chat and streaming?
[05:12] Priya Patel: yes streaming and multi-turn are available in the hosted API during the trial. streaming incurs the same token calculations.
[05:18] Sara Chen: we need to measure end-to-end latency from our edge to the decoder. any suggestions?
[05:23] Priya Patel: include network RTT in your test, use our SDK with direct region selection, and test with both small sequences (short prompts) and longer sequences. we'll provide sample harnesses including curl and python. we recommend running at multiple qps and with batching configs to see tradeoffs.
[05:40] Alex Rivera: curious about billing granularity. per token? rounding?
[05:44] Jordan Kim: billed per token with transparent breakdown. console shows token-level cost and latency per request so you can attribute cost to routes. batching reduces per-token inference cost but watch latency impact.
[05:56] Sara Chen: any pitfalls customers hit when moving from hosted to dedicated?
[06:01] Priya Patel: we see three main areas: 1) different perf profile because you're on reserved hardware, so kernel selection and quant configs may differ; 2) networking changes — private networks add complexity; 3) operational runbook changes — autoscaling policies need tuning. we help with a migration checklist.
[06:20] Jordan Kim: for procurement timelines, if you need Dedicated or Private it usually takes longer due to contract and provisioning; hosted can start immediately.
[06:29] Alex Rivera: that aligns with our thinking. we'd like to start with hosted to move fast, then evaluate Dedicated if cost or SLOs require it.
[06:38] Priya Patel: perfect. for benchmarking, if you can share 3 representative prompts and a small dataset, we'll run a quick hosted benchmark, then propose a dedicated config if needed.
[06:48] Sara Chen: ok i'll get that to you. one more question: can we restrict model versions and pin a rollout for canary?
[06:56] Jordan Kim: yes — Redwood supports model version pinning, canaries, and automatic fallback policies. Console allows rollout configs per route.
[07:06] Tom O'Neill: what's the SLA on hosted?
[07:09] Jordan Kim: hosted has a standard uptime target; SLA-backed uptime and latency targets are part of Dedicated/Enterprise tiers. we can share the SLA doc.
[07:17] Alex Rivera: great. anything on data residency? some customers require EU-only data handling.
[07:22] Priya Patel: we have region selection for the hosted API and Private deployments can be provisioned in-region; for strict residency we recommend Private with customer-managed networking.
[07:32] Sara Chen: ok. can you email the security pack and SOC2 report?
[07:36] Jordan Kim: yes we'll send SOC2, pen test summary, and our security whitepaper.
[07:41] Alex Rivera: perfect. next steps?
[07:44] Jordan Kim: Jordan to send pricing + quickstart links; Priya to share benchmark checklist and runbook; schedule a technical deep dive with Tom for latency tests; Alex to provide prompts. we'll aim for those due dates next week.
[07:57] Speaker 2: great, thanks everyone.
[08:00] Jordan Kim: thanks all, we'll follow up via email with links and scheduling.
[08:05] End of recording.
